focused_question_template: Does attacker-controlled input reach the matched-against string of a regex whose pattern (`{callee_name}`) has a structurally confirmed catastrophic-backtracking-prone shape (nested quantifier, or an alternation branch with a quantified portion followed by more content)? Note: this classification is a structural heuristic, not a formal proof of worst-case complexity -- verified against empirically-measured real cases, not assumed from pattern shape alone.

whether the regex engine in use has any mitigations (e.g. V8's linear-time fallback for simple patterns, RE2-style engines) not modeled by this property
